summary: The workflowcheck tool causes Out-of-Memory errors on large codebases by eagerly loading and caching all classes from the entire classpath (potentially 20,000+ classes) when searching for workflow implementations, even though only a few classes are actually workflows.
userImpact: Developers working with large codebases cannot run workflowcheck in CI without hitting Out-of-Memory errors that block their build pipelines.
rootCause: The ClassPath constructor eagerly enumerates and loads every class file from the entire classpath using ASM ClassReader, storing all ClassInfo objects in a HashMap for the lifetime of the scan. This wastes memory by loading thousands of non-workflow classes that are never needed.
proposedFix: Two approaches: (1) Add --scan-classpath flag to enumerate classes only from specified scan paths while maintaining full classpath for dependency resolution, loading only classes encountered during call-chain tracing. (2) Implement two-pass lazy loading with annotation filtering - quick scan for WorkflowInterface/WorkflowMethod annotations first, then full ASM analysis only on matched classes.
keyQuote: For a project with a few workflow classes buried among ~20,000 dependency classes, the tool eagerly loads all 20,000 just to find those few classes.
